verifiedEvidence: The question text matches the official original. It asks for the power [W] dissipated in R=10 Ω.
Choices (1) 0.28, (2) 1.89, (3) 3.79, (4) 5.36 and (5) 7.62 all match the original.
The official answer table lists 理論 問5 as 1, which matches officialAnswer="1".
Node equations: 6VA−4VB=60 gives 3VA−2VB=30, and 8VB−6VA=80 gives 4VB−3VA=40. Adding them gives 2VB=70, so VB=35 V and VA=100/3 V.
I_R=(100/3−35)/10=−1/6 A, so the current flows from B to A with magnitude 1/6 A. P=(1/6)²×10=10/36≈0.2778 W, which rounds to 0.28 W, choice (1).
The KCL check at A gives −0.667+0.833−0.167=0. The KCL check at B gives −0.75+0.583+0.167=0. Both balance.
Reversing either source gives about 13.6 W, which is not among the choices. This supports reading both long plates as the top (positive) terminals.
Each wrong choice has its own back-calculation: 1.89 W needs 0.435 A, 3.79 W needs 0.616 A, 5.36 W needs 0.732 A and 7.62 W needs 0.873 A. All of these are correct and none equals 1/6 A.
The public candidate figure keeps every label (60 V, 40 Ω×2, R=10 Ω, 60 Ω×2, 80 V), the junction dots and both source polarities. It is enough on its own to solve the problem.

If both 3 V and 4 V were reversed, 7V=31.2 gives V≈4.457 V and R≈4.86 Ω. This matches the distractor (4), so the explanation of choice (4) correctly names the specific mistake behind it.

verifiedEvidence: The question text matches the original: E [V], internal resistance r [Ω], R1 [Ω] and variable R2 [Ω] in parallel, find R2 that maximises Joule heat. The original page has no circuit diagram, so figureUrls=[] is correct.
Choices (1) R2=r, (2) R2=R1, (3) rR1/(r+R1), (4) rR1/(R1−r) and (5) rR1/(r−R1) all match the original.
The official answer table lists 理論 問7 as 3, which matches officialAnswer="3".
Thevenin equivalent seen from R2: V_th=E·R1/(r+R1) and R_th=r∥R1=rR1/(r+R1). Maximising P=V_th²R2/(R_th+R2)² gives R2=R_th, choice (3).

Choice (2): when R1=r the required value is r∥R1=R1/2≠R1, which is correct. Choice (5): r<R1 makes R2 negative, which is correct. Choice (4): the denominator can be 0 or negative, and the expression is not the parallel combination. Choice (1): R1 is ignored. All of these are correct.

verifiedEvidence: The question text matches the original: two LC series resonant circuits A and B with resonant frequencies f_A and f_B, and f_AB after connecting them in series.
Choices (1) f_A<f_B<f_AB, (2) f_A<f_AB<f_B, (3) f_B<f_AB<f_A, (4) f_AB<f_A<f_B and (5) f_AB<f_B<f_A all match the original.
The official answer table lists 理論 問8 as 3, which matches officialAnswer="3".
LC products: A=LC, B=2LC. In series, L=3L and C=C/2, so the product is 1.5LC, which agrees with the zero-reactance condition ω²·3L=2/C. Since f∝1/√(LC), f_B<f_AB<f_A.
Numerical check with LC=1: f_A=0.159, f_AB=0.1299≈0.130, f_B=0.1125≈0.113. All correct.
Each wrong choice has a specific reason. (1) makes f_A the smallest and f_AB the largest. (2) reverses the order. (4) and (5) make f_AB the smallest. All of these explanations are correct.
The public candidate figure keeps circuits A (L, C), B (2L, C) and the series circuit (L, C, dot, 2L, C), with all terminals and all labels. It is enough on its own to solve the problem.
